summary:
NASA Agro-Bolivia is a geospatial decision-support web platform and Telegram alert system designed to protect agricultural productivity and soil health across Bolivia’s 343 municipalities. By integrating NASA FIRMS active fire hotspots, MapBiomas Bolivia Collection 4 agricultural land-use masks, and real-time NASA POWER climatology APIs (T2M_MAX, PRECTOTCORR, and GWETROOT root-zone soil wetness), the platform bridges the gap between raw satellite telemetry and actionable field decisions.

Built with a FastAPI backend and an interactive React + Leaflet web map, the system enables farmers, agronomists, and local authorities to inspect municipal wildfire threats or click any exact GPS parcel coordinate to evaluate heat stress, precipitation deficits, soil moisture, and fire proximity. Users can generate printable technical PDF field reports with custom branding, use offline-ready local caching in low-connectivity rural areas, and receive automated alerts via Telegram. This empowers vulnerable farming communities to prevent crop loss, optimize irrigation, and mitigate wildfire damage.
details:
What It Does & How It Works NASA Agro-Bolivia is an interactive geospatial decision-support platform and automated alert system covering all 343 municipalities in Bolivia. Users can search any municipality or click an exact GPS parcel coordinate on a satellite map to evaluate wildfire proximity and agro-climatic stress in real time. The backend cross-references NASA FIRMS active fire hotspots (2025) with MapBiomas Bolivia Collection 4 agricultural land-use masks to separate agricultural burn risks from forest fires, while querying the NASA POWER Climatology API for maximum temperature (T2M_MAX), corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), and root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT).

Key Benefits & Expected Impact Rural farmers, agronomists, and municipal emergency teams often lack technical tools to interpret raw Earth observation data. Our platform translates complex satellite telemetry into plain-language agronomic recommendations, downloadable official PDF field reports, and instant Telegram bot alerts. By providing early warnings for drought, heat stress, and encroaching wildfires—even in low-connectivity areas via local offline caching—the project helps smallholder communities prevent crop loss, optimize irrigation scheduling, and protect soil health.

Tools, Languages & Software Stack

  • Data & Geospatial Processing: Python (GeoPandas, Shapely, PyProj), ArcMap, NASA FIRMS, NASA POWER API, and MapBiomas Bolivia Collection 4.
  • Backend & Messaging: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Requests, python-dotenv, and the Telegram Bot API (deployed on Render).
  • Frontend & Reporting: React, Vite, Leaflet.js with Esri World Imagery satellite tiles, custom printable PDF report generator, and offline local caching (deployed on Vercel).

Creativity & Design Considerations Rather than building a generic fire tracker, we creatively combined land-cover classification with root-zone soil moisture and exact GPS parcel diagnostics—delivering insights through a zero-friction web interface and Telegram, a lightweight messaging app already widely used on low-bandwidth mobile networks across rural Bolivia. Our team specifically designed the system around offline resilience, lightweight GeoJSON payloads for fast loading on mobile data, and printable PDF reports for local agricultural cooperatives.
